header: The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
above the first "section" line before the game starts, and an area's section when the area first draws with its
shaders, so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
Recorded by code, not by playing: bash tools/record_shaders.sh (its header says how) runs N64Recomp-browser's
tools/record_shaders.mjs with tools/shader_plan.json, which loads the page fresh for each section. Section 0 is the
launcher and the boot: the logos, the start of the intro story and the title, reached with Start as a player does.
Then tools/shader_survey.js plays the intro story whole from the title (intro()) and the attract demo whole (demo():
twelve maps and five battles), and a new file is started from file select with A as a player does and its prologue
played with A until its first battle. Then the pause menu, its tabs gone through with the stick, A and B, in Toad
Town. Then a section an area: from a new file's first map (left out), warp() goes to each of a few of its maps as an
exit does, at that chapter's point in the story (GB_StoryProgress), and Mario walks each for 10 s of the game's time:
the Goomba Region, Toad Town, its sewers, the Koopa Region, the Koopa Bros. Fortress, Star Haven, Mt. Rugged, Dry
Dry Outpost and Desert, Dry Dry Ruins, Forever Forest and Boo's Mansion, Gusty Gulch and Tubba Blubba's Castle, Shy
Guy's Toy Box, the whale and Lavalava Island, Mt. Lavalava, Flower Fields, the Shiver Region, Crystal Palace,
Bowser's Castle, Peach's Castle and its grounds, and the minigames. Not recorded: battles other than the demo's and
the prologue's, the chapters' cutscenes and bosses, and the ending. Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR, MSAA,
upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording again.
